title: OMS User Guide for Traders
body:
OMS User Guide for Traders
Owner: Daniel Reyes, Head of Trading
Last updated: 2026-07-29
Audience: Trading desk (equity traders, sales traders, execution traders, trading associates, quants with order entry rights)

Purpose
This guide covers day-to-day use of the OMS, the order management system for the trading desk, and how it connects to the TradeBlotter. It is a working reference, not a policy document. Where it conflicts with the Compliance or Risk manuals, those manuals win. No client names or account identifiers belong in free-text fields in the OMS; this guide therefore contains none, and you should not add any to order notes.

System Dependencies You Should Know
The OMS depends on PricingSvc for instrument prices and on AuthSSO for login and entitlements. The TradeBlotter depends on both the OMS and PricingSvc. In practice this means:
- If AuthSSO is degraded, you may be unable to log in or your entitlements may fail to load. Do not share sessions or credentials; raise it in #it-ops.
- If PricingSvc is stale, reference prices and limit checks in the OMS may be wrong, and blotter P&L will drift. Treat any price flagged stale as untradeable for limit-sensitive orders.
- Downstream, the SettlementEngine consumes executed trades from the OMS, so a booking error here becomes a settlement break later.

Logging In and Entitlements
Log in through AuthSSO with your firm credentials and MFA. Entitlements are role-based: execution traders can route and amend, sales traders can enter and allocate on behalf of coverage, trading associates have enter and cancel-own rights only, and quants have read access plus staged-order entry for approved strategies. Requests for changes go to your desk head, then to Technology via the access ticket queue. Entitlement changes are not instant; allow one business day.

Entering an Order
1. Open the order ticket and select the instrument from the security master. Confirm the identifier, not just the ticker.
2. Choose side, quantity, order type (market, limit, VWAP, TWAP, or participation), and time in force.
3. Select the book. Principal, agency, and wealth flow books are separate; picking the wrong one is the most common booking error we see.
4. Add a short, factual note if needed. Keep it to the order rationale or instruction reference.
5. Submit. Pre-trade checks run automatically against position and notional limits and restricted-list status.

Pre-Trade Checks and Overrides
Hard blocks cannot be overridden by traders. Soft warnings, such as notional above the single-order guideline or a price deviating more than the tolerance from the last reference price, require a written acknowledgement. If an instrument is on the restricted or watch list, stop and contact Compliance in #compliance before doing anything else. Repeated overrides are reviewed weekly by me and by Market Risk.

Amending and Cancelling
Amendments to quantity or limit price create a replace request with the venue. Until the venue confirms, the order shows as pending replace; do not resend. If you see a pending state lasting more than a minute, call the execution desk before cancelling, to avoid a double fill.

Allocations
Block orders are allocated after the fill using the allocation template on the ticket. Sales traders own allocations for their coverage. Allocations must be complete before the end-of-day cutoff so that the SettlementEngine picks up the correct splits. Late or partial allocations should be flagged to Operations the same day.

Using the TradeBlotter
The TradeBlotter is the live view of your orders, fills, positions, and intraday P&L. Key points:
- P&L is computed from OMS fills and PricingSvc marks. It is indicative, not the official book of record. Official P&L comes from the finance close.
- Use the filter bar to scope by book, desk, or strategy. Saved views are personal; the shared views maintained by the desk are read-only.
- If a fill appears in the OMS but not on the blotter within a few seconds, refresh once, then report it. Do not re-enter the trade.
- Exporting the blotter to a spreadsheet is permitted for desk analysis only. Do not send exports outside the firm.

End-of-Day Checklist
- All working orders are either cancelled or intentionally carried (GTC) with a note.
- Allocations complete and unmatched fills cleared.
- Blotter positions agree with your own tally for the books you run.
- Any breaks or manual adjustments are posted in #trading-desk or passed to Operations, who reconcile them in #recon.

When Things Go Wrong
For an OMS outage or order routing failure, call the desk head first, then post in #incidents with the time, the affected books, and the order references involved. Use the voice execution fallback only with approval from me or the senior execution trader on shift, and log every manually executed trade so it can be booked once the OMS is back. For slowness or access problems that are not outages, use #it-ops.

Training and Questions
New joiners complete an OMS walkthrough with an execution trader in their first week and are signed off before live order entry. Questions about this guide or suggestions for changes can go to me directly. Changes to checks and limits are made only through Risk and Compliance approval and are announced on #trading-desk.
